## The fix (single wire-contract fix → all platforms)
`ProjectionRevTracker::stamp_app_owned_revs`: for app-owned (non-manifest) keys, derive a content-driven rev — a per-key counter that increments when the payload fingerprint changes — so the rev advances iff content changed. Cleared rows keep 0; Tier-2 built-ins untouched. Now `chirp.timeline.home` emits rev 1 (empty) → rev 2 (cards), so the host guard `2 <= 1` is false → it decodes the card frame → renders. Fixes iOS + Android + web at once (no per-platform host patch needed). [...] 1. CORRECTNESS vs contract — SOUND. Note the ADR situation first: post-ADR-0073 reset, docs/decisions/0070-typed-read-sessions.md no longer contains any Rung/projection_rev text, and ADR-0055 no longer exists on disk; the durable rev contract now lives in the emission-ladder code itself (crates/nmp-core/src/kernel/projection_rev/mod.rs header + rung2_stamp.rs). That contract: monotonic u64 per key, advances when content changes, Rung 3 omits Unchanged. Built-ins derive rev from SourceVersions write-chokepoint counters ("option C — NOT content-hash-as-gate", mod.rs:25-37). The PR uses a content-fingerprint gate for app-owned keys — a deliberate divergence, and the right one: the kernel has zero write-chokepoint visibility into host-registered projections (opaque payload bytes from run_typed_projections, update.rs:289), so content is the only available signal. It's actually a tighter approximation of "content changed" than the built-ins' source-sum. Both mechanisms satisfy the property hosts depend on: rev never stays flat across a content change.

2. EMISSION LADDER — NO REGRESSION, strictly better. Rung 3 (kernel/update/rung3_omit.rs:63-70) decides omission from MANIFEST PRESENCE, never from entry.projection_rev; keys absent from the manifest default to Changed and are "always kept, never omitted (D3-7)". App-owned keys can never enter the manifest (build_manifest at projection_rev/mod.rs:392 enumerates exactly KERNEL_BUILTIN_PROJECTION_KEYS, test-enforced by build_manifest_covers_all_builtin_keys). So wire emission counts for app-owned keys are byte-for-byte unchanged; the only behavioral delta is host-side: unchanged payloads now keep their prior rev so rev-aware hosts correctly skip re-decode (an improvement — before the bug, they wrongly skipped everything; the naive alternative would wastefully re-decode every tick since app-owned rows are emitted every tick). [...] `ProjectionRevTracker::stamp_app_owned_revs`: for app-owned (non-manifest) keys, derive a content-driven rev — a per-key counter that increments when the payload fingerprint changes — so the rev advances iff content changed. Cleared rows keep 0; Tier-2 built-ins untouched. Now `chirp.timeline.home` emits rev 1 (empty) → rev 2 (cards), so the host guard `2 <= 1` is false → it decodes the card frame → renders. Fixes iOS + Android + web at once (no per-platform host patch needed). [...] 4. FINGERPRINT MECHANISM — sound. DefaultHasher over payload bytes is deterministic in-process; per-key (u64 rev, u64 fp) slots in a HashMap keyed by projection key — correctly scoped, no cross-key sharing (test-covered). Kernel is a single-threaded actor with &mut self, so no concurrency hazard. Monotonic for the kernel's lifetime: the tracker is created once (kernel_new.rs:235) and app_owned_revs is never reset (reset_last_emitted doesn't touch it — correct). The `rev == 0 || last_fp != fp` bump means a Changed row never carries rev 0, and A→B→A content toggles keep advancing (1,2,3). The Cleared→Changed edge is safe: Cleared rows skip the slot (keep rev 0 on the wire), and the host cache REMOVES the entry on Cleared (swift_projection_cache.rs:236-238 doc: "Cleared row → remove from cache"), so a subsequent Changed at an unchanged rev is admitted (cache[key] is nil). Epoch/session change: host caches do a mandatory reset (D4, swift_projection_cache.rs:224) while kernel revs persist — safe in both directions. Residual risks are negligible: a 64-bit hash collision between consecutive distinct payloads would delay one frame until the next change (~2^-64, same risk class as every fingerprint gate already in this file, e.g. diagnostics_payload_fingerprint); the map never prunes Cleared keys (tiny tuples, bounded by distinct feed keys opened per session — and keeping them is the monotonicity-safe choice if a host ever misses a Cleared). [...]    - app_owned_revs: documented that Cleared entries are never pruned (monotonicity over memory) so a re-opened key resumes above its last-emitted rev.
